provenance.source: UN WPP 2024 (population) + ILO/World Bank (participation) + Penn World Table 10.01 (productivity) + EU KLEMS 2023 (sector productivity/deepening/source labour shares) + IEA WEO 2024/NGFS (emissions intensity)
provenance.licence: see per-entry sources; UN WPP: CC BY 3.0 IGO, PWT 10.01: CC BY 4.0, ILOSTAT/WB: CC BY 4.0, EU KLEMS: CC BY 4.0
provenance.notes: Documented, sourced per-region and per-sector annual growth trajectories for the Phase 7b.2 structural drivers, ASSEMBLED FROM data/structural/sources/inputs.json by scripts/build_structural_trajectories.py (pipeline step 1a — reproducible, not hand-edited). v2 adds source_labour_shares (source-period labour shares s_L^src for the source-side MFP identification, review P1 2026-09-06). Rates are decimal fractions per year, entered as dated knots from the cited published figures; the wrapper holds the most recent knot piecewise-constant. Regions are the model's illustrative multi-region labels N (North, a developed-economy proxy) and S (South, an emerging-economy proxy) plus a global __all__ default; on a real EXIOBASE build these map to actual country/region trajectories via the same loader. Figures remain illustrative headline values, not consulting-grade extractions — see docs/structural-data-pipeline-plan.md.

sources.population:N: UN World Population Prospects 2024, Medium variant — annual population growth rate for high-income regions (approx +0.3%/yr 2025 declining to negative by 2050). https://population.un.org/wpp/
sources.population:S: UN World Population Prospects 2024, Medium variant — annual population growth rate for less-developed regions (approx +1.2%/yr 2025 declining toward +0.5%/yr 2050). https://population.un.org/wpp/
sources.population:__all__: UN World Population Prospects 2024, Medium variant — world annual population growth (approx +0.8%/yr 2025 to +0.3%/yr 2050). https://population.un.org/wpp/
sources.labour_participation:N: ILOSTAT / World Bank labour-force participation modelled estimates — high-income economies: broadly flat, mild decline with ageing. https://ilostat.ilo.org/
sources.labour_participation:S: ILOSTAT / World Bank labour-force participation modelled estimates — emerging economies: mild rise from rising female participation, tapering. https://ilostat.ilo.org/
sources.labour_participation:__all__: ILOSTAT / World Bank global labour-force participation — approximately flat/mild rise. https://ilostat.ilo.org/
sources.productivity:N: Penn World Table 10.01, TFP growth at constant national prices (rtfpna) — advanced economies ~1.0-1.2%/yr trend. Feenstra, Inklaar & Timmer (2015), AER; https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/
sources.productivity:S: Penn World Table 10.01, TFP/labour-productivity growth — emerging economies convergence ~2.2-3.0%/yr trend. Feenstra, Inklaar & Timmer (2015), AER; https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/
sources.productivity:__all__: Penn World Table 10.01, world-average productivity growth ~1.7%/yr. Feenstra, Inklaar & Timmer (2015), AER; https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/
sources.sector_productivity:BRD: EU KLEMS 2023 release — sectoral labour-productivity growth; goods-producing/manufacturing sectors run above the economy average (~1.5%/yr). https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.sector_productivity:MIL: EU KLEMS 2023 release — services/mixed sectors run below the goods average (~0.8%/yr). https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.sector_productivity:__all__: EU KLEMS 2023 release — economy-average sectoral labour-productivity growth ~1.0%/yr. https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.emissions_intensity:BRD: IEA World Energy Outlook 2024 / NGFS Net Zero 2050 — carbon-intensive sectors decarbonise ~3%/yr near-term accelerating to ~5%/yr toward mid-century. https://www.iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2024 ; https://www.ngfs.net/ngfs-scenarios-portal/
sources.emissions_intensity:__all__: IEA WEO 2024 / NGFS Net Zero 2050 — economy-wide CO2 intensity of GDP declines ~2%/yr near-term to ~3.5%/yr mid-century. https://www.iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2024 ; https://www.ngfs.net/ngfs-scenarios-portal/
sources.capital_deepening:BRD: EU KLEMS 2023 release — sector capital services per hour worked (g_K/L); capital-intensive goods-producing/manufacturing sectors deepen ~1.0-1.2%/yr. Used to net capital deepening out of observed labour productivity via the Cobb-Douglas finite-change mapping 1+g_phi = [(1+g_Y/L)/(1+g_K/L)^s_K]^(1/s_L). https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.capital_deepening:MIL: EU KLEMS 2023 release — services/mixed sectors deepen more slowly (~0.6%/yr capital services per hour). https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.capital_deepening:__all__: EU KLEMS 2023 release — economy-average capital deepening ~0.8%/yr (capital services per hour worked). https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.source_labour_share:BRD: ILLUSTRATIVE headline source-period labour share of value added for goods-producing/manufacturing archetype (~0.58). Placeholder for an EU KLEMS adjacent-period Törnqvist labour cost share; see docs/structural-data-pipeline-plan.md step 1b. https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.source_labour_share:MIL: ILLUSTRATIVE headline source-period labour share for services/mixed archetype (~0.62, more labour-intensive). Placeholder for an EU KLEMS Törnqvist share; see docs/structural-data-pipeline-plan.md step 1b. https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
sources.source_labour_share:__all__: ILLUSTRATIVE economy-average source-period labour share (~0.60). Placeholder for an EU KLEMS Törnqvist share; see docs/structural-data-pipeline-plan.md step 1b. https://euklems-intanprod-llee.luiss.it/
